newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fremantle port to take days to return to normal.
newsitem.headline: Fremantle port to take days to return to normal.

text.p: Fremantle port is likely to need "some days" to return to normal after a 24-hour strike over proposed industrial relations legislation, a port spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
Fremantle is the fourth largest container port in Australia.
On Tuesday, tugs in both the inner and outer harbour did not operate and stevedores stopped work in protest at changes to Western Australia's Labour Relations Act.
Ainslie de Voss, the port's public affairs manager, said one vessel - a sheep carrier - was exempted from the stoppage but nine other vessels were subject to delays of up to 24 hours.
"The men returned to work this morning and it is quite a scene of activity at the moment with everyone trying to catch up the backlog," she said.
"Twelve ships are affected today - three delayed berthings, five delayed departures plus delays in cargo handling on four ships.
"It could be some days before we are back to normal."
The Labour Relations Legislation Amendment Bill is still being debated in the Legislative Council but is expected to be passed by that house by tomorrow.
It will then require ratification in the Legislative Assembly because of 27 amendments agreed to by the government in the face of trade union opposition to the bill.

A government spokesman said more talks were held on Tuesday night between the Premier Richard Court, Labour Relations Minister Graham Kierath, and the state Trades and Labour Council which is co-ordinating the protest campaign.
The spokesman said, however, there was no breakthrough achieved.
"There's been no change," the spokesman said. "They thrashed out a few ideas but nothing resulted from that regarding changes to government policy or industrial action," he said.
An estimated 1500 public servants marched on Parliament House on Wednesday to express their opposition to the legislation.

In other related developments, striking milk workers are to meet later on Wednesday to vote on a union recommendation that they return to work to avoid the need for dairy farmers to dump large quantities of milk for which they have no storage.
